technologyTransitions.title: US Technology Transitions restrictions (AIM Act) — 40 CFR 84.54
technologyTransitions.verified: 2026-09-28 against the eCFR text as reproduced by Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/40/84.54)
technologyTransitions.appliesTo: Only products/systems using a 'regulated substance' (one of the 18 HFCs listed in the AIM Act, 42 U.S.C. 7675(c)) or a blend containing one. Pure HFOs/HCFOs, hydrocarbons, R-717, R-744, CFCs, HCFCs and PFCs are not regulated substances.
technologyTransitions.gwpBasis: 40 CFR 84.64: exchange values (appendix A) for regulated substances; blends = sum of constituent GWP x nominal mass fraction (84.64(b)); constituents without a listed GWP are excluded (84.64(c)). Compare the refrigerant's headline (US EPA basis) GWP against 'gwpAtLeast'.

restrictionTypes.manufacture_import: 84.54(a): No person may manufacture or import any product in the listed subsector that uses a regulated substance as listed.
restrictionTypes.sale_distribution: 84.54(b): Effective three years after each (a) date, no person may sell, distribute, offer for sale or distribution, or export any product that uses a regulated substance as listed in (a).
restrictionTypes.installation: 84.54(c): No person may install any system (or have it installed as its designer, owner, or operator) in the listed subsector that uses a regulated substance as listed.

technologyTransitions.installationDefinition: 84.54(e): upon charging the system to full charge, installation includes (1) assembling a system for the first time from used or new components; (2) increasing the cooling capacity (BTU/h) of an existing supermarket system by more than 15 percent, or increasing the cooling capacity of any other type of existing system; (3) replacing 75 percent or more of evaporators (by number) and 100 percent of the compressor racks, condensers, and connected evaporator loads of an existing system.
technologyTransitions.permitExtension: 84.54(d): the installation compliance date is extended one year for industrial process refrigeration systems with a January 1, 2026 compliance date and for the retail food — supermarket, cold storage warehouse and ice rink subsectors when an approved building permit issued prior to October 5, 2023 specifies the restricted refrigerant.
technologyTransitions.servicing: 84.54 restricts new manufacture/import, later sale/distribution, and installation (as defined in 84.54(e)). Servicing and repairing existing equipment is not an 'installation' unless it meets 84.54(e).
technologyTransitions.matching: Match 'named' lists by exact designation; normalize 'HFC-134a' -> 'R-134a', 'HFC-227ea' -> 'R-227ea'. Ignore list items the dataset does not contain.

section608.leakRepairNote: No general federal rule bars adding refrigerant to a leaking system. Leak-repair duties apply by appliance size: 40 CFR 82.157 (appliances with 50 lb or more of class I/II refrigerant) and 40 CFR 84.106 (from January 1, 2026: appliances with 15 lb or more of HFC refrigerant with GWP above 53; residential and light-commercial AC and heat pumps exempt).

applianceDefinitions.highPressure: Liquid phase saturation pressure between 170 psia and 355 psia at 104 °F. Examples: R-22, R-407A, R-407C, R-410A, R-502.
applianceDefinitions.mediumPressure: Liquid phase saturation pressure between 45 psia and 170 psia at 104 °F. Examples: R-114, R-124, R-12, R-134a, R-500.
applianceDefinitions.lowPressure: Liquid phase saturation pressure below 45 psia at 104 °F. Examples: R-11, R-123, R-113, R-245fa.
applianceDefinitions.veryHighPressure: Critical temperature below 104 °F or liquid phase saturation pressure above 355 psia at 104 °F. Examples: R-13, R-23, R-503, R-508A, R-508B.
applianceDefinitions.smallAppliance: Fully manufactured, charged, and hermetically sealed in a factory with five pounds or less of refrigerant (e.g. refrigerators and freezers, room air conditioners including window, portable and PTAC units, dehumidifiers, under-the-counter ice makers, vending machines, drinking water coolers). Small appliances are outside Table 1.

article13_3.text: From 1 January 2020, the use of fluorinated greenhouse gases, with a global warming potential of 2 500 or more, to service or maintain refrigeration equipment with a charge size of 40 tonnes of CO2 equivalent or more, shall be prohibited. This paragraph shall not apply to military equipment or equipment intended for applications designed to cool products to temperatures below – 50 °C. The prohibition shall not apply until 1 January 2030 to (a) reclaimed fluorinated greenhouse gases with a GWP of 2 500 or more used for the maintenance or servicing of existing refrigeration equipment, provided that they have been labelled in accordance with Article 12(6); (b) recycled fluorinated greenhouse gases with a GWP of 2 500 or more used for the maintenance or servicing of existing refrigeration equipment provided they have been recovered from such equipment.

montrealProtocol.kigaliAnnexF: The Kigali Amendment (2016) added HFCs as controlled substances in Annex F (Group I: 16 HFCs; Group II: HFC-23) with a phase-down under Article 2J. HFOs and HCFOs are not listed.
montrealProtocol.cfcDevelopingCountries: Developing (Article 5) countries phased out CFC production by 2010; developed countries on January 1, 1996.
montrealProtocol.ozoneRecovery: 2022 Scientific Assessment Panel: with current policies the ozone layer is expected to recover to 1980 values by around 2066 over the Antarctic, 2045 over the Arctic and 2040 for the rest of the world.
